decks.notes: This Orzhov Control deck focuses on using a variety of spells and creatures to control the game and outvalue opponents. The deck includes cards that disrupt opponent strategies, remove threats, and generate card advantage. It also features a mix of removal spells, creatures with powerful abilities, and lands that provide additional utility. By utilizing a combination of control tools and resilient threats, this deck aims to dominate the battlefield and grind out incremental advantages until victory is assured.

The main idea of this deck is to quickly establish a strong board presence and apply pressure on the opponent using aggressive creatures and removal spells. The deck aims to control the board with cards like Go for the Throat and Make Disappear, while simultaneously building an army with cards like Dennick, Pious Apprentice and Raffine, Scheming Seer. Sheoldred, the Apocalypse can be a game-winning threat if left unchecked. The mana base allows for consistent access to all colors needed for spells and creature abilities.

Utilize a combination of counterspells, removal, and card advantage to control the game and outvalue your opponent. Use disruptive spells like Disdainful Stroke and Void Rend to hinder your opponent's game plan, while maintaining card advantage with cards like Memory Deluge. Sheoldred's Edict and Go for the Throat provide efficient removal options, and Farewell serves as a versatile tool for dealing with various threats. The mana base is structured to support the deck's Control strategy, with a mix of dual lands and utility lands to ensure consistent access to all necessary colors of mana.

The main focus of this deck is to aggressively deal damage to the opponent as quickly as possible using a combination of cheap, efficient burn spells and aggressive creatures. The deck aims to control the board and pressure the opponent with a mix of direct damage and creature threats, leveraging cards like Bloodthirsty Adversary, Play with Fire, and Lightning Strike. With a strong mana base and support from key cards like Kumano Faces Kakkazan and Feldon, Ronom Excavator, this deck aims to overwhelm opponents before they can stabilize.

This deck focuses on controlling the game by utilizing a combination of counterspells, removal spells, and powerful board wipes to keep the opponent's threats in check. It also employs card advantage and recursion through cards like Memory Deluge and The Wandering Emperor. The mana base is designed to ensure smooth color access for the Esper color combination, allowing for flexibility in casting spells of different colors. With a mix of disruption and card advantage, this deck aims to outlast the opponent and take control of the game.

The main focus of this deck is to control the game by disrupting the opponent's strategy and resources while building up card advantage. The deck includes various counterspells and removal spells to deal with threats, along with card draw effects to maintain hand advantage. The mana base is designed to support the control strategy, with a mix of lands that provide different colors of mana and potentially untapped sources. Overall, the deck aims to outlast opponents and grind out victories through attrition and careful resource management.

The main concept of this deck is to overwhelm the opponent with a swarm of low-cost, aggressive creatures, while also disrupting their game plan with cards like Thalia, Guardian of Thraben and Destroy Evil. The deck also aims to generate value through cards like Recruitment Officer and Adeline, Resplendent Cathar, while maintaining a strong board presence with cards like Steel Seraph and Coppercoat Vanguard. Overall, the strategy revolves around building a fast, powerful army and applying constant pressure to the opponent to secure a quick victory.

This Esper Control deck focuses on disruption and removal spells to control the game until the late game, where it can take over with powerful finishers like The Wandering Emperor and Memory Deluge. The deck includes a mix of counterspells, removal spells, and card draw to maintain board control and outvalue the opponent. The mana base is designed to support the three-color combination of white, blue, and black while also providing flexibility and consistency in casting spells. Overall, the deck aims to outlast the opponent and grind out a victory through attrition.

The mana base allows for flexibility and consistency in playing both black and blue spells to control the board and maintain pressure on the opponent.
